statement: A path holding an encoded `;` (`%3B`) or an encoded control character (`%00` to `%1F`, `%7F`), in either case of the hex digits and anywhere in the path, path parameters included, is answered 400 before authentication, mapped route or not: CoSec reads them as text of a segment, but a backend that decodes before it strips path parameters, stops at NUL or drops what follows a control character serves another path than the one decided. A raw control character is answered the same way, whichever server hands the path over; a raw `;` is a path parameter. A double-encoded one (`%253B`, `%2500`) decodes to text, and a trailing dot or space is read as written.
guards: runtime:EncodedPathTest#an encoded semicolon or control character is refused before authentication, with its event
